metadata.title: Main Bhi Bharat।PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TRIBAL GROUPS (PVTG) GOING HUNGRY ।आदिवासियों में बढ़ी भूख
metadata.description:
A recent study has revealed that the tribal population, especially the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) have been the worst affected by the covid-induced lockdown. 77% of these tribals do not have enough food to eat. This study also says that women and children from the PVTGs  are the most affected. This study was conducted in 11 states of India.

transcription_english: [00:00:10.000] The Covid-induced lockdown forced 77% of the country's most
[00:00:16.383] vulnerable tribes to eat less.
[00:00:22.914] The tribal people of the country have had to
[00:00:25.750] bear the brunt of the Covid lockdown.
[00:00:28.709] 56% of the people who lost their source of income in the months of
[00:00:34.208] April and May still have no means of earning money.
[00:00:40.240] And this has had a direct impact on their ability to buy food.
[00:00:46.000] 77% of those from the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
[00:00:50.169] have reduced the amount of their daily food intake.
[00:00:55.000] Around 75 tribal communities in India fall under the category of PVTG,
[00:00:59.827] which means 75 communities are still backward on
[00:01:03.350] social, economic and educational levels,
[00:01:07.356] and for whom government makes special schemes.
[00:01:11.360] During lockdown, hunger and malnutrition was found
[00:01:14.505] to be higher among children, youth,
[00:01:17.051] and pregnant and lactating women from these communities.
[00:01:22.561] Actually, the biggest source of income of PVTG tribes is
[00:01:27.106] forest produce,
[00:01:29.481] which they sell in markets of nearby cities to earn money.
[00:01:34.122] They do not own land for farming.
[00:01:37.211] But during the 4-5 months of lockdown there
[00:01:40.614] was no way for them to sell the produce collected from the forests
[00:01:45.461] the markets were closed, so they had no income.
[00:01:50.240] A survey conducted by the NGO Right to Food Campaign
[00:01:54.335] among 4,000 people in 11 states has found that
[00:01:58.643] 54% of the tribals' food consumption was reduced in the lockdown.
[00:02:04.000] Before lockdown, where these people did not sleep hungry at night,
[00:02:08.642] now one in seven had no choice but to stay hungry.
[00:02:14.828] The RTF survey also found that the quality of consumption of the
[00:02:19.320] poor and backward classes has fallen during lockdown.
[00:02:24.222] Among those who used to consume eggs and meat before
[00:02:28.438] lockdown, 91% said they can no longer do so.
[00:02:33.658] About 73% said they had reduced green vegetables in their diet,
[00:02:39.660] and 64% said they had to cut down on lentils.
[00:02:44.011] Another problem for tribals is that most of them do not have
[00:02:48.656] ration cards, or even if they do it does not contain
[00:02:52.379] the names of all family members.
[00:02:54.800] This reduces the amount of food they receive from ration shops.
[00:03:01.524] Many tribals also migrate for labour, and for this reason
[00:03:06.330] their ration card gets cancelled after some time.
